Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

Moses-and-Joshua exchange about the 'SOUND OF UNFERMENTED WINE' during the Sinai golden-calf episode — a WITTY GEʽEZ ETIOLOGICAL moment unique to Meqabyan within the Pentateuchal-reception tradition. The exchange exegetes Exodus 32:17-18 (Joshua hearing 'the noise of war in the camp' / Moses replying 'it is not the voice of them that shout for mastery, neither is it the voice of them that cry for being overcome: but the noise of them that sing do I hear') by giving the 'singing' a specifically intoxicated tonality. The chapter as a whole retells the Flood-Noah covenant (vv. 1-3) + the Decalogue in five-commandment form (vv. 7-9) + the golden-calf narrative (vv. 11-18). The five-commandment Decalogue summary is itself a distinctive EOTC catechetical form.

candidates.draft_body:
Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

DECALOGUE IN FIVE-COMMANDMENT FORM (vv. 7-9) — a DISTINCTIVE EOTC CATECHETICAL FORM compressing the standard ten commandments (Exodus 20:1-17 / Deuteronomy 5:6-21) into five. The five-fold structure typically pairs related commandments: 1-2 (no other gods + no graven images) + 3 (no taking-the-name-in-vain) + 4 (Sabbath) + 5 (honor parents) + 6-10 (against killing/adultery/stealing/false-witness/coveting). The Tewahedo Catechism (Ḫaymanot Abäw + Mäṣḥafä Qǝddasē) preserves both the standard ten-form AND the five-form pedagogically. The five-form's compression facilitates oral-catechesis-by-memory and may reflect the Geʽez-liturgical-rhythmic preference for five-fold structures (cf. Five Pillars of the Tewahedo faith + five-cycle Tewahedo-week-pattern in the Sǝnkǝsar). The verse anchors the Decalogue specifically within the Meqabyan-frame of covenant-faithfulness-against-idolatry.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

GOLDEN-CALF AT HOREB (vv. 11-18) — direct Exodus 32 narrative retelling with the distinctive Meqabyan-Geʽez witty exchange between Moses and Joshua about the 'sound of unfermented wine' (v. 15 — see seed 14:15). The full narrative encompasses: Aaron's calf-making at the people's demand (v. 11) + Moses's intercession for Israel (v. 13) + the broken-and-restored tablets cycle (v. 16 ff.) + Levitical-sword-judgment (v. 17 ff.). The Meqabyan retelling FRAMES the golden-calf as the paradigmatic apostasy-in-the-very-moment-of-revelation — the same pattern Ṣiruṣaydan's kingdom enacts at imperial scale. Direct echo of Psalm 106:19-23 ('they made a calf in Horeb, and worshiped the molten image. Thus they changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass'). Tewahedo liturgical-tradition cites Exo 32 / Psa 106 at the Lenten-and-fasting commemorations of apostasy-as-cycle.
